claims.text: Alloys or compounds containing short-range-order precipitates can be used for lattice heat conductivity applications.
A hierarchical microstructure can be designed to scatter phonons at specific frequencies.
The proposed material is initially a crystalline solid.
Creating a hierarchical microstructure is the intervention used to produce frequency-specific phonon scattering.
Lattice heat conductivity is significant at low temperatures.
Short-range-order precipitates are the structural mediator.
Phonon scattering by short-range-order precipitates reduces thermal conductivity.
The proposed microstructure will reduce thermal conductivity by 10–20% relative to alloys or compounds without short-range-order precipitates.
The proposed effect applies over a temperature range of 100–500 K.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction depends on alloy or compound identity and microstructure design.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify low temperatures, whereas the stated boundary extends to 500 K, which is not consistently characterized as a low-temperature regime.

The predicted reduction is 10–20%, but the falsification rule only rejects reductions below 5%; an observed reduction between 5% and 10% would contradict the quantified prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
